newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate up to 14 pct from 12.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate up to 14 pct from 12.8 pct.

text.p: High volume of term loans pushed up the Croatian average lending rate to 14.0 percent on Thursday from 12.8 percent previously in livelier trade and amid continued good liquidity, dealers said.
They put the daily trade at 26.8 million kuna, up from 15.4 million the previous day. The end of trading left a surplus of almost 150 million on the supply side.
Fresh deals accounted for 19.3 million kuna. All banks were positive and borrowers sought only term loans, one dealer told Reuters.
Call money loans, usually dominating the transactions, amounted to only 500,000 kuna, granted at a lower rate of seven percent.
New one-month loans were granted at 12 and 13 percent.
Two- and three-month loans, which made up most of Thursday's trade were struck at 18 percent.
Banks rolled over previous loans at 9-10 percent for two week and 19 percent for three-month deals.
The central bank calculated its kuna midrates for Friday and Monday firmer at 6.5226 against the dollar and at 3.5701 against the German mark. -- Zoran Radosavljevic, Zagreb Newsroom +385 1 455 7075
